title: Senior Backend Engineer
dek: Harbor's billing pipeline processes usage events for about 400 customers. You'd own the parts that decide what they get charged.
description: Harbor Analytics sells metering and billing infrastructure to companies that charge by usage — API calls, compute minutes, seats that fluctuate monthly. Our core pipeline ingests roughly 40 million events a day, aggregates them against each customer's pricing model, and produces an invoice that has to be right, because when it's wrong, someone's finance team calls us.

You'd join the 6-person Ledger team, which owns the aggregation and invoicing services (Go, Postgres, Kafka). Recent work included rebuilding our proration logic after a customer's mid-cycle plan change produced a negative invoice line, and adding idempotency keys to the event ingestion path after a retry storm double-billed three accounts for an afternoon. That's the kind of bug you'd be the second or third person to look at.

We ship to production several times a day behind feature flags, and every engineer carries a rotation week roughly once every six weeks. On-call pages are rare but not theoretical — you should be someone who wants to understand why a query plan changed, not just restart the pod.
requirements: 5+ years building backend services in a strongly typed language — ours is Go, but strong Java, C#, or Rust experience transfers
Have worked directly with a system where correctness had a dollar amount attached to it (billing, payments, ledgers, inventory)
Comfortable reading and writing non-trivial SQL against Postgres — we don't use an ORM for the ledger tables
Can explain a production incident you were involved in and what changed afterward, not just that it got fixed
Experience with Kafka or an equivalent event stream is a plus, not a requirement — we'll teach the specifics
